newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen posting small rise - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen posting small rise - trade.

text.p: Far East metal traders said on Tuesday copper stocks on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are seen posting a small rise of about 1,000-2,000 tonnes although trading will remain quiet until after the New Year holiday.
The stocks report is due out at 0900 GMT on Tuesday.
Aluminium stocks, which rose in the December 20 report by 6,350 tonnes and then slid 4,175 tonnes on December 24, will probably remain unchanged to 1,000 tonnes lower, they said.
"One thousand to two thousand tonnes up for copper sounds just about right," one Singapore dealer said. "But most people are away on holidays so it's going to be very, very quiet."
"There's just no trading being done at all," a dealer in a Europe metal trading firm added.
One trader said he was about to leave his office.
"I'm about to go. There's no use being here," he said.
No one in the offices of two Japanese metal trading houses picked up the phone and the answering machine in one said leave a message and we will get back to you after the New Year.
"We're closing down after midday. We'll just sit here and count down the minutes before leaving," one dealer said.
Only a small amount of copper has not been placed on warrant with the LME's Singapore warehouse while there was no report of any further material being shipped to warehouses here.
The volume of copper in the LME warehouse in Singapore reached 28,850 tonnes in the report on December 24, up 3,900 tonnes from the December 20 report.

Three month copper prices were being quoted as steady by regional dealers at 0200 GMT at around US$2,125/30 a tonne, when compared with a late London indication on Monday of $2,129. Aluminium prices were seen slightly higher at 0200 GMT at $1,552/57 a tonne against late trade in London yesterday of
